question: Reported in an NVIDIA Senior Software Engineer interview: write a custom `malloc` whose returned memory is aligned to a given size. The report does not say whether to build on the system allocator or to write a new allocator, so state both readings: a wrapper around `malloc`, and aligned allocation inside your own pool.
lookingFor: Bit-mask alignment arithmetic and power-of-two validation
Handling free correctly via a stored header
Thinking about overhead, overflow and fragmentation
Knowing the standard APIs and when to prefer them
followUps: Why does adding align - 1 and masking round up?
How would you return the unused leading gap to the allocator?
What alignment does plain malloc guarantee and why?
How does aligned allocation relate to false sharing?
